artifacts.summary: Grounds the hook-registration orphan sweep in merge.lua's existing remove_orphaned_index_entries precedent and call-siting, reconciles the hook_identity()/lint identity divergence, and directly re-verifies all claimed live instances across five real deployed repos (finding Logos/Theory's prior hand-repair incomplete and a new cross-event defect shape).

memory_candidates.content: This repo's extension loader (lua/neotex/plugins/ai/shared/extensions/) already has a working orphan-sweep precedent for merge-target content removal: merge.lua's remove_orphaned_index_entries, called from init.lua's manager.load per-extension loop immediately BEFORE process_merge_targets re-adds that extension's own fresh entries, using a valid-set-excluding-self pattern. Any new merge-target orphan sweep (e.g. for settings.json hook registrations) should mirror this exact call-siting and convergence property rather than inventing a new one, since it is already proven order-independent across a resync_all loop.

merge.lua's hook_identity() (hooks/*.sh only) and lint-hook-registration-paths.sh's normalize_identity() (any invoked script path, ~/-anchored paths explicitly exempt) are a documented, deliberate divergence in this codebase (lint script's own D4 comment). A ~/-anchored hook command (e.g. claude-ready-signal.sh invoked as ~/.config/nvim/scripts/claude-ready-signal.sh) is identity-ineligible under both today and must stay ineligible under any broadened/reconciled identity function -- it is a real, externally-provided integration point found live in three deployed repos, not a hypothetical edge case.

A hook-registration drift shape exists that current tooling/tasks do not name: the same hook script surviving registered under a DIFFERENT EVENT (e.g. stale PostToolUse copy alongside a current PreToolUse registration), not just a different matcher within one event. deep_merge in merge.lua processes each top-level hooks.<EVENT> array independently, so nothing compares across events. Observed live in Logos/Theory's validate-no-task-references.sh (runs twice per Write/Edit as a result). Worth checking for when evaluating any hook-registration health/drift question in this codebase.
